source.title: Where Do LLM Values Come From?

record.file_problem: The text is complete, but some mathematical expressions and numerical values are missing from the supplied rendering, including the reported PCA variance fractions.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines value rankings and value-vector structure, but does not test convergence of input representations, any of the listed claim versions, or their dependence on scale or similarity metrics.
record.gate_note: The study reports shared structure in value representations, including PCA results and qualitative directions across models. These concern representations of evaluated values, not whether independently trained models induce increasingly similar distances between the same inputs. No results are included from cited work.
record.test_reason: The post predicts post-training value changes from data representations. Its PCA of value vectors within each model, and its qualitative note that Llama8B and Olmo7B-SFT show similar 'safe vs. non-safe' and 'emotion vs. logic' directions, do not measure alignment between models' representations of the same inputs. There is no cross-model similarity metric, no scale trend, no mapping or stitching, and no seed comparison. It neither tests nor relies on representation convergence, so it is T6. 'discusses' overstates the link, since the topic is never discussed; the closest relation is cites_only, though it does not cite the originals either.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that value changes can be partly predicted from dataset representations: embeddings work well for SFT, activations work better for DPO and narrow datasets. Much of this signal may reflect a shared refusal/safety latent factor, and the overall results are called somewhat inconclusive. They draw no conclusions about representation convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates and predicts post-training value changes; it does not apply a representation-convergence method.

fits_no_version.finding: Two different models (Llama8B and Olmo7B-SFT) qualitatively show similar top value-vector PCs: a 'safe vs. non-safe' direction and an orthogonal 'emotion vs. logic' direction. Value vectors share a large component, tied to refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Value-vector representations in different LLMs share similar dominant axes (safety/refusal, emotion vs. logic).

record.problems: The PCA variance fractions are missing in the supplied rendering. The reported representational analysis concerns value vectors and does not quantify alignment of model representations on shared inputs.

untested.parts: All of it; the similar value directions across Llama8B and Olmo are qualitative and not about features or circuits

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only' (nearest fit for a T6 paper with no engagement with the claim). This is a LessWrong post and is unrelated to the phenomenon.

versions.untested_parts: Scale-related convergence of independently trained models' input representations.
Cross-modal image-caption representation alignment as models improve.
Feature or subspace convergence across random seeds of the same architecture.
Mapping, stitching, or other interchangeability of model representations.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Dependence of representation convergence on similarity metric settings or input distribution.
Whether representation alignment is incomplete or explained by shared data or objectives.
